First time in China and not sure where to begin? Here are 10 places that deserve a spot on your list.

Eat: Peking Duck, Zhajiang Noodles
2. Shanghai · The Futuristic Metropolis
Don't Miss: The Bund, Lujiazui Skyline, Yu Garden

3. Xi'an · The Ancient Capital

4. Chongqing · The Cyberpunk Mountain City
Don't Miss: Hongya Cave, Liziba Monorail, Yangtze River Cableway
Eat: Spicy Hot Pot

Don't Miss: Giant Panda Breeding Base, Jinli Ancient Street, Wuhou Shrine
Eat: Sichuan Hotpot, Dan Dan Noodles, Mapo Tofu
6. Guangzhou · The Food Capital
Don't Miss: Canton Tower, Chen Clan Academy, Yongqing Fang
Eat: Dim Sum, Claypot Rice, Roast Goose, Double-Skin Milk
7. Harbin · The Ice Kingdom
Don't Miss: Ice and Snow World, St. Sophia Cathedral
Best Time: December – February ❄️
8. Yunnan · The Land of Eternal Spring
Don't Miss: Erhai Lake (Dali), Old Town of Lijiang, Tiger Leaping Gorge, Stone Forest
Eat: Across-the-Bridge Noodles, Steam Pot Chicken, Grilled Milk Fan
9. Hangzhou · Heaven on Earth
Don't Miss: West Lake, Lingyin Temple, Longjing Tea Village

10. Zhangjiajie · Avatar Mountains
Don't Miss: Zhangjiajie National Forest Park, Tianmen Mountain, Glass Skywalk

China is a fascinating place, but it can be overwhelming if you're not prepared! Here are some essential tips to make your trip smoother:
1. Download Amap for navigation since Google Maps won't help you here.
2. High-speed trains are often better than flying for city-to-city travel.
3. Cash is becoming obsolete; use Alipay or WeChat Pay for convenience.
4. Be cautious with power banks at airports; they can be confiscated if not marked properly.
5. Avoid using foreign cards for payments over 200 RMB to dodge extra fees.
6. Don't rely solely on translation apps; screenshotting menus works better.
7. Explore local markets and neighborhoods for the best experiences!
China is easier than it seems once you have the basics sorted. Happy travels!

contents.desc: Chinese factories produce 75% of the world’s toys. These factories are mostly located in Southern China. The center of toy production used to be in Hong Kong in the 1960s, but by the 1980s, most companies moved to Southern China to take advantage of lower labor costs. In 2004, photographer Michael Wolf traveled to Southern China to document the lives of workers: their endless days of sewing, painting, and packaging, as well as glimpses of their humanity — how they sleep, eat, and live under the conditions of global consumerism and capitalism. #madeinchina #china #capitalism #toys #consumerism #factories #chinesefactory #laborrights #workerrights #photography #history #manufacturing #chinesehistory
